title: PulseBench: tokens/sec microbenchmark harness for core inference models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build PulseBench: a focused, CI-integrated tokens-per-second microbenchmark harness for our core served models. Goal: provide reproducible, low-noise measurements of sustained tokens/sec and p95 tail latency across model variants and infra permutations, and to detect regressions automatically with a rolling-baseline regression detector. Deliverables include a workload generator (sustained/step/burst modes), telemetry extractor (tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99, GPU util, kv-cache metrics, batch distribution), CI jobs (quick smoke + nightly endurance), and an automated alert/bisect entrypoint when regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: A1: PulseBench repo with documented workload modes (sustained, stepped, burst) and config templating for model, sequence length, concurrency, and kv-cache warmup
A2: CI smoke job runs on PRs and produces a concise HTML+JSON report uploaded to artifacts (tokens/sec time-series + p95 table)
A3: Nightly long-run (1h sustained) runs and writes results to perf-store with metadata tags (model, commit, region, infra-type)
A4: Regression detector runs nightly and alerts Slack + creates a draft bisect issue when p95 or tokens/sec deviates beyond configured thresholds (default: p95 +15% or tokens/sec -12%)
A5: Dashboard tile in Console perf-space showing last 30 days for core models and linking to raw run artifacts
A6: Integration tests that simulate 3 different concurrency patterns and validate reported metrics within expected noise bounds
implementation_notes: We will implement PulseBench in Go for lightweight concurrency and easy binary distribution; a thin Python wrapper will exist for local developer runs and parameter exploration
Workload generator should model real customer patterns: 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-256), 10% long (>256), with configurable mixture per run
KV-cache warmup is critical: provide a prefill phase to reach steady-state cache hit ratios and an explicit warmup_shards parameter
Use existing telemetry exporter (metrics-agent) to emit named metrics: pulsebench.tokens_per_sec, pulsebench.latency.p95, pulsebench.kv_hit_ratio, pulsebench.batch_size_histogram
Avoid adding model-internal instrumentation; rely on observability surface already provided by runtime and augment with synthetic trace IDs for correlating requests
test_plan: Unit tests for workload generator and metrics aggregator
Integration smoke that runs against a dev cluster with a tiny model (5M params) to validate end-to-end reporting
Nightly long-run job in CI that runs on dedicated staging capacity and pushes artifacts to perf-store bucket
Introduce controlled regression in staging (increase latency via artificial sleep) to validate detector and alert flow
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): land repo, basic workload modes, CI smoke (1 week)
Phase 2 (staging): add nightly runs, integrate with perf-store, add dashboard tile (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (prod-watch): enable adaptive thresholds and automated bisect workflow, onboard 3 core models and 2 infra permutations (1 week)
Canary approach: start with shadow runs (no traffic impact) and a 7-day parallel evaluation before enabling alerts to oncall
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed for Go workload generator. Prototype can sustain 10k tokens/sec on local workstation with synthetic model stub.
2026-03-05: Telemetry schema draft posted (link below). Chose pulsebench.* metric namespace to avoid collisions.
2026-03-08: CI smoke action created (github.com/redwood/pulsebench/actions). Smoke runs currently 30s workload and uploads JSON artifact.
2026-03-10: Nightly runner integration started; perf-store schema decision: each run writes metrics.json + aggregated-summary.json and a small flamegraph if latency > baseline
review_feedback: PM (R. Chen): prioritize stable p95 signal over raw tokens/sec; include median+iqr in reports
Infra (L. Gomez): require opt-in for running long nightly jobs on Dedicated until autoscaling quotas are validated
Design (M. Liu): report format should include a 1-line verdict (OK/WARN/REGRESS) to make triage faster for oncall
notes: Noise reduction strategy: use median of 5 short runs for quick CI feedback and a single long-run for authoritative baseline
Detector algorithm: rolling-window baseline (14 days) + parameterized sensitivity to avoid flapping; implement a cooldown of 48h before opening bisect
Tolerance: configurable per-model; default thresholds tuned from historical traces of core models
Follow-up: plan to add cross-model comparison in later iteration to catch regressions introduced by shared kernel changes
next_steps: Finish Go binary and release v0.1 in pulsebench repo
Wire smoke CI to create Linear artifact on failure with triage checklist
Create dashboard tile in Console perf-space and link to run artifacts
